title: Rethinking the Use of Tests: A Meta-Analysis of Practice Testing
sample: Practice-testing experiments across educational and laboratory contexts
population: Learners represented in the included studies
mainFinding: Practice testing generally improved learning relative to restudy and other non-testing conditions, with meaningful moderators.
limitations: Effects vary with test format, feedback, population and outcome.
elosRelevance: Supports active retrieval while requiring context-sensitive policy and feedback.

title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis
mainFinding: The spacing interval and desired retention interval jointly affect later recall.
limitations: The synthesis centers on verbal recall and does not prescribe one universal interval.
elosRelevance: Supports spaced review and rejects a fixed schedule as universally optimal.

title: The Effects of Spaced Practice on Second Language Learning: A Meta-Analysis
mainFinding: Spaced practice showed a medium-to-large benefit; longer spacing was more useful on delayed tests than shorter spacing.
limitations: Effects were moderated by target, practice, feedback and retention interval.
elosRelevance: Supports spaced technical-English retrieval without a vocabulary-only product model.

title: The science of effective learning with spacing and retrieval practice
sample: Review of laboratory and applied educational research
population: Learners across ages and domains represented in the literature
mainFinding: Spacing and retrieval practice support retention and transfer across many settings.
limitations: Implementation conditions and educational context matter.
elosRelevance: Supports a combined retrieval-and-spacing policy with observable outcomes.

title: Calibrating calibration: A meta-analysis of learning strategy instruction interventions to improve metacognitive monitoring accuracy
mainFinding: Learning-strategy instruction improved monitoring accuracy on average.
limitations: Effects varied by setting, age, strategy and judgment design.
elosRelevance: Supports comparing confidence judgments with actual performance, never using confidence alone as mastery.

title: Synthesizing Results From Empirical Research on Computer-Based Scaffolding in STEM Education: A Meta-Analysis
mainFinding: Computer-based scaffolding supported outcomes in problem-centered STEM learning.
limitations: Only a minority of synthesized outcomes included fading, so strong universal fading claims are unsupported.
elosRelevance: Supports bounded assistance with cautious, evidence-triggered fading.

title: Similarity Matters: A Meta-Analysis of Interleaved Learning and Its Moderators
sample: 238 effect sizes in 158 samples from 59 papers, N=8466
population: Learners across category and problem-learning studies
mainFinding: Interleaving effects depend strongly on the similarity and type of learning material.
limitations: The average benefit does not justify random mixing of unrelated topics.
elosRelevance: Supports interleaving only explicit confusion pairs.

title: Inducing Self-Explanation: a Meta-Analysis
population: Learners studying texts, worked problems and problem solving
mainFinding: Self-explanation prompts produced a positive average effect with substantial contextual moderators.
limitations: Prompt type, task, domain and duration vary; fluent text does not guarantee correct explanation.
elosRelevance: Supports prompts scored against explicit semantic invariants.

title: Transfer of test-enhanced learning: Meta-analytic review and synthesis
sample: 192 effect sizes from 122 experiments in 67 reports, N=10382
population: Learners across retrieval and transfer experiments
mainFinding: Retrieval practice can support transfer, but effects depend on congruence, elaboration and transfer type.
limitations: Transfer was weak or absent in some conditions and cannot be inferred from retrieval success alone.
elosRelevance: Supports recording transfer as separate, stronger evidence.

title: A Stochastic Shortest Path Algorithm for Optimizing Spaced Repetition Scheduling
sample: Large-scale spaced-repetition interaction logs; replication data published by the authors
population: Users represented in the MaiMemo logs
mainFinding: A memory model and stochastic shortest-path policy reduced modeled memorization cost against reported baselines.
limitations: Algorithmic benchmark evidence does not establish effectiveness for ELOS tasks or its richer evidence model.
elosRelevance: Supports an FSRS-related baseline for simulation, not a production replacement without local calibration data.

title: Linguistic Constructs Represent the Domain Model in Intelligent Language Tutoring
sample: Pilot use by hundreds of university learners reported by the authors
learningDomain: explicit linguistic constructs in intelligent tutoring
mainFinding: Typed constructs can organize exercises, feedback and learner-progress modeling.
limitations: A system demonstration does not establish causal learning gains from a concept graph.
elosRelevance: Supports a small explicit relation model with provenance rather than inferred KG-RAG.

title: LECTOR: LLM-Enhanced Concept-based Test-Oriented Repetition for Adaptive Spaced Learning
mainFinding: The paper reports a simulated improvement over several scheduling baselines.
limitations: Preprint, synthetic evaluation, no evidence of effectiveness for real ELOS learners, and an external-LLM privacy cost.
elosRelevance: Recorded as experimental context only; no LLM scheduler is adopted.

title: Broccoli: Sprinkling Lightweight Vocabulary Learning into Everyday Information Diets
sample: See the peer-reviewed paper for the reported study details
mainFinding: The system explores embedding lightweight vocabulary encounters in everyday reading.
limitations: The evidence does not justify inserting vocabulary into every ELOS activity or treating exposure as mastery.
elosRelevance: Experimental design reference only; no automatic insertion adopted.

title: Pedagogical Word Recommendation: A novel task and dataset on personalized vocabulary acquisition for L2 learners
sample: Dataset collected through an ITS serving approximately one million TOEIC learners
population: L2 learners using the source ITS
mainFinding: The paper defines a word-knowledge prediction task and baseline dataset.
limitations: Prediction performance is not evidence that recommendations improve learning outcomes.
elosRelevance: No neural recommender adopted; explicit evidence and professional relevance remain primary.
